questions.text: You can smell perfume from across the room even though you cannot see it in the air. This is evidence that matter is:
options: Made of tiny particles too small to see
questions.explanation: Matter is made of particles too small to see. Perfume particles spread through the air, so you can smell it from far away.

questions.text: A 100 gram ice cube melts completely into water. How much does the water weigh?
questions.explanation: Matter is conserved when it changes state. The melted water still weighs 100 grams, the same as the ice.

questions.text: Which property could you use to tell whether a material is a metal like iron?
questions.explanation: Materials can be identified by their properties. Being attracted to a magnet is a property that helps identify metals like iron.

questions.text: You mix baking soda and vinegar, and it bubbles and fizzes into a new gas. This shows that:
questions.explanation: When mixing two materials makes bubbles, heat, or a color change, a new substance may have formed. The fizzing gas is a new substance.

questions.text: You drop a ball off a table. Which way does it fall, and why?
options: Down, because gravity pulls it toward Earth's center
questions.explanation: Gravity is a force that pulls objects down toward the center of the Earth, so a dropped ball falls straight down.

questions.text: A rabbit eats grass to get energy. Where did the energy in the grass originally come from?
questions.explanation: The energy animals use for their bodies comes from food, and that energy can be traced back to the Sun, which plants use to grow.

questions.text: A tree grows much larger over many years. Where does MOST of the material that makes it bigger come from?
questions.explanation: Plants get most of the material they need to grow from air (carbon dioxide) and water, not mainly from the soil.

questions.text: In a food web, what is the role of a decomposer like a mushroom?
options: It breaks down dead matter and returns nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals, recycling matter and returning nutrients to the soil for plants to use.

questions.text: In a meadow food web, grass is eaten by grasshoppers, which are eaten by frogs. If all the grass died, what happens FIRST?
questions.explanation: Food webs show how energy moves between living things. Without grass, the grasshoppers that eat it lose their food first.

questions.text: The Sun looks much bigger and brighter than other stars. Why?
options: It is much closer to Earth
It is the only real star
It is made of fire only
questions.explanation: The Sun appears larger and brighter because it is much closer to Earth than other stars, which are very far away.

questions.text: Why do we have day and night on Earth?
options: Earth rotates, or spins, on its axis
The Sun turns off at night
questions.explanation: Earth spins on its axis once about every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day; the side facing away has night.

questions.text: A shadow from a pole is long in the early morning and short at noon. This daily pattern is caused by:
options: The changing position of the Sun in the sky
questions.explanation: As Earth rotates, the Sun's position in the sky changes, so shadows change length and direction in a daily pattern.

questions.text: Wind blowing over the ocean pushes waves onto a beach and moves sand. This is an example of two Earth systems interacting: the
questions.explanation: Earth's systems interact. Here the atmosphere (moving air/wind) affects the hydrosphere (ocean water) and the geosphere (sand).

questions.text: About what fraction of Earth's water is FRESH water that people can use for drinking?
options: A very small amount; most is salty ocean water
questions.explanation: Most of Earth's water is salty ocean water. Only a small amount is fresh water, and much of that is frozen in ice.

questions.text: Which action would BEST help protect Earth's environment?
questions.explanation: People can protect Earth's resources. Recycling and conserving water reduce waste and harm to the environment.

questions.text: You have two clear liquids. One conducts electricity and one does not. This test helps you:
options: Tell the two liquids apart by their properties
questions.explanation: Measuring properties, like whether a liquid conducts electricity, lets you identify and tell materials apart.

questions.text: An engineer has three possible designs for a water filter. What is the BEST way to choose one?
options: Compare how well each meets the goals, then pick the best
questions.explanation: Engineers compare designs against the criteria, or goals, and choose the one that best meets them.

questions.text: Tree roots growing into a rock slowly crack it apart over many years. This shows the geosphere interacting with the:
questions.explanation: The biosphere is all living things. Tree roots (biosphere) breaking rock (geosphere) shows these Earth systems interacting.
